command: llvm-mc -triple=aarch64 -filetype=obj A64-P16-loadlit.s -o out.o && llvm-objcopy -O binary --only-section=.text out.o out.bin
notes: Input (104 B, LF, trailing newline). The source is two labels plus six loads in the plan's order: `.L1:` / `ldr x0, .L2` / `ldr x1, #-4` / `.L2:` / `ldr x2, #1048572` / `ldr x3, #-1048576` / `ldr x4, .L1` / `ldr x5, #4`. `.L1` is offset 0 and `.L2` is offset 8, so the two symbol targets are the same two instruction addresses the plan's symbols name (S1 = 0, S2 = 8) and the same `(S, P)` pairs reach the field: 8 and -16 bytes. `llvm-mc` resolves local labels itself, so `llvm-readobj -r` prints an empty relocation list and no linker is involved. The four value rows state `imm19` field content in 4-byte units (`-1`, `262143`, `-262144`, `1`), which is why `#-4` and `#4` in the source are the field values `-1` and `1`: the assembler spells the byte offset, the plan states the field (ADR-0023 decision 3). Labels on instruction addresses keep the vector one section with no data fragments; the fixup arithmetic is the same one a data target would use.
source: Arm MRS LDR_64_loadlit (opc = 01, imm19 at 5+19, Rt at 0+5, no Rn), measured in EXP-0025 §1-§3
